title: Greece Handed Down
question: How did ancient Greece and Rome shape the world after them?
hook: A culture that began with poems and city-states went on to shape law, politics and philosophy for the modern world.
idea: The Romans preserved and spread Greek culture, and surviving fragments of it later helped spark the Renaissance.

beats.prompt: The Romans came to rule lands where Greek art, philosophy and education were already admired. What did they mostly do with that culture?

choices.label: Replace it with a wholly new Roman culture
choices.feedback: It tempts because conquerors often impose their own ways, but the Romans preserved and imitated Greek culture.

choices.label: Preserve it, imitate it and spread it across Europe
Ban it in the lands they ruled
choices.feedback: It tempts because empires fear rival cultures, but the Romans spread it throughout Europe.

choices.label: Keep it only within Greece itself
choices.feedback: It tempts because it sounds tidy, but Roman spread carried it throughout Europe.

beats.explain: The Romans preserved, imitated, and spread Greek culture throughout Europe.

beats.prompt: Put these events in order, earliest first.
items: The Senate votes never again to allow a king (509 BC)
Death of Alexander the Great (323 BC)
Fall of the Western Roman Empire (476 AD)
beats.explain: Rome's legendary founding came first, then the Senate's vote, then Alexander's death, and finally the fall of the Western Empire in 476 AD.

beats.prompt: Match each Greek event to its result.
pairs: Ended with Athens dominant in the Delian League
Ended Spartan supremacy and brought Theban hegemony
Reign of Philip II (359 to 336 BC)
Macedon expanded into Paeonian, Thracian and Illyrian lands
beats.explain: Each event shifted which power led Greece, from Athens to Sparta to Thebes to Macedon.
The Dark Ages lost writing and used geometric pottery, while the Archaic period brought democracy, philosophy and the Orientalizing style.
